description: LinkedIn Ads provides a REST API for programmatic access to advertising functionality, including ad account management, campaign management, and reporting, authenticated via OAuth 2.0.

access.credential_access: Client ID and Client Secret obtained from the LinkedIn Developer Portal after creating an app

buildability.blocker: Access to the Advertising API requires submitting an access-request form and approval; generic data collection use cases are rejected.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn Ads uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication.
Access to the LinkedIn Marketing/Advertising API runs through a vetted Developer app and 3-legged OAuth.
Marketing/Ads APIs require 3-legged OAuth (acting on behalf of a member). The 2-legged client-credentials flow is explicitly not allowed for Ads.
LinkedIn Ads exposes user management through the `/rest/adAccountUsers` collection under the Marketing API, authenticated via OAuth 2.0.
OAuth 2.0 is used for authentication, with steps including registering an application, requesting scopes, and exchanging an authorization code for an access token.
For server-to-server flows, use the 2-legged OAuth (client credentials) flow if your app is approved for it.
Include the access token in all API requests as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
The LinkedIn Ads API uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication.
To use the LinkedIn Ads API, developers typically authenticate using OAuth 2.0.
LinkedIn Ads provides a REST API.
LinkedIn Ads utilizes a REST API for programmatic access to advertising functionality.
The LinkedIn Ads API has webhooks (called 'push events' or 'notifications').
There is no LinkedIn Ads 'API key.' You create a LinkedIn Developer app, get approved for the Advertising API, and use 3-legged OAuth to get access tokens.
Access is gated: you submit an access-request form describing your use case, and LinkedIn reviews it. Generic data collection gets rejected; ads management and reporting use cases get approved.
To create a developer app, you need a LinkedIn account and a LinkedIn Company Page.
A Client ID and Client Secret are generated after you create a new developer app.
